AbstractText.Label: OBJECTIVE
AbstractText.content: To evaluate the clinical outcome of palliative surgery using posterior decompression and fixation combined with intra-operative vertebroplasty (PDFIV) for the treatment of spinal metastases, and analyze the indications for PDFIV using a neurologic, oncologic, mechanical, and systemic (NOMS) framework.

AbstractText.Label: SUMMARY OF BACKGROUND DATA
AbstractText.content: Palliative surgery is widely used to spinal metastatic patients with poor condition for enough postoperative recovery. PDFIV which is a new palliative surgery is rarely reported its efficacies and indications.

AbstractText.Label: METHODS
AbstractText.content: A retrospective analysis of 26 consecutive patients with spinal metastases treated by PDFIV was performed. The group includes 18 men and 8 women with an average age of 55.7 years (range, 47-79). All patients presented with local pain, 18 patients had compressive myelopathy, and nine had radiculopathy. The total segments involved were 32. Post-operative imaging was used to evaluate cement leakage, the status of fixation, and recurrence. The VAS score and Frankel grade were used to identify neurologic function.

AbstractText.Label: RESULTS
AbstractText.content: There were no intra-operative neurologic or vascular injuries. The mean operative time was 173 minutes (range, 125-245 min), the mean blood loss was 659 mL (range, 350-2500 mL), and the average amount of cement used in the vertebrae was 4.1 mL (range, 2.0-5.5 mL). All patients were followed for an average of 25 months (range, 6-56 mo). The VAS score decreased from 8.1 pre-operatively to 2.1 post-operatively. Fifteen of 18 patients with compressive myelopathies had improved Frankel grades. Post-operative CT scans showed cement leakage in three patients (11.5%); however, all of the leakages were clinically asymptomatic. There were local tumor recurrences requiring re-operation in 2 patients.

AbstractText.Label: CONCLUSION
AbstractText.content: Palliative surgery using PDFIV can improve neurologic function and alleviate pain effectively, and allow low cement leakage and timely disposal of leakage combined with intra-operative visual vertebroplasty.
